The tour at a glance

- **4** departures in 2027
- **9** riding days
- **1** rest day in Toulouse
- **11** nights

- The route is the same on every departure.
- Groups run with a minimum of 6 riders. The target is 8, and the maximum is 12.
The route and the week
From the Atlantic to the Mediterranean, the tour passes through these stops:

- Bordeaux
- La Réole
- Agen
- Moissac
- Toulouse (rest day)
- Castelnaudary
- Carcassonne
- Lézignan-Corbières
- Capestang
- Sète
How the week runs

- **Friday** Arrive in Bordeaux. Collect a rental e-bike if you booked one.
- **Saturday** Ride briefing at breakfast, then wheels roll in the morning.
- **Nine riding days** The group rides the canal path from Bordeaux to Sète, with one rest day and two nights in Toulouse.
- **Monday** Final group night in Sète.
- **Tuesday** Guests are on their own from the morning.
Dinner in Toulouse
The second evening in Toulouse includes a dinner at a Michelin restaurant. Dress expectation: a collared shirt such as a polo for men, and business-casual clothing for women.

Bordeaux Airport to Gare Saint-Jean: tram or airport bus
How to get from Bordeaux Airport (Mérignac) to Gare Saint-Jean station and nearby hotels: Tram Line F or the 30'Direct airport bus, with times, costs, and bike rules.
Practical information
Bordeaux Airport to Gare Saint-Jean and your hotel
Gare Saint-Jean is Bordeaux's main railway station. All recommended hotels are within about 500 m of the station.
Schedules and fares come from the transport operators and were last checked in June 2026. Confirm them with TBM and 30'Direct before you travel.
Your two options
Tram Line F

- Cost: €1.90
- Travel time: about 45 minutes
- Frequency: every 10–15 minutes
- Bike in a case: always allowed
- Tickets: TBM app or machines
- Best for: lowest cost and flexibility
30'Direct airport bus

- Cost: €9–10
- Travel time: about 30 minutes
- Schedule: limited window
- Bike in a case: accepted
- Tickets: online or onboard
- Best for: fastest public option
Which should I choose?
Choose Tram Line F if:

- Lowest cost matters
- You arrive early or late
- You have a bike case
- You want flexibility
Choose the 30'Direct airport bus if:

- Fastest journey matters
- You arrive during operating hours
- Extra cost is okay
- You want the simplest trip
Details
What is it?
Direct tram connection from Bordeaux Airport (Mérignac) to Gare Saint-Jean (main train station). Launched Dec 6, 2025.
Direct coach shuttle from Bordeaux Airport to Gare Saint-Jean. No intermediate stops, no transfers.
How often does it run?
Every 10 min (Mon–Sat) / Every 15 min (Sun/holidays). First: ~5am. Last: Midnight (Mon–Wed), 1am (Thu–Sat)
Limited: 07:30–20:05 daily. Mon–Fri: ~22 runs. Sat/Sun: ~14 runs. Not available early morning or late evening.
How long does it take?
~45 minutes. Direct, no transfers.
~30 minutes (traffic dependent)
How much does it cost?
€1.90 per ticket
€9 online / €10 on board
What about my bike?

✅ Bikes in cases: Always
✅ Bikes not in cases: 9am–4pm only
❌ NOT 7am–9am or 4pm–7pm
Pack in case to avoid rush hours.
TBM Bicycle Rules: 05 57 57 88 88

✅ Bikes in cases: Yes
✅ Bikes not in cases: Yes
Requirement: Closed bag, labeled with name, phone, address.
Carrier may refuse oversized items.

30'Direct FAQ: 30direct.com
How do I book?

No booking required. Buy ticket at tram stop (vending machine), TBM mobile app (Bordeaux transit app), or Relay newsstand at airport.

To board: Validate your ticket on the platform or onboard validators (card readers, white validators, or TBM app via Bluetooth). Self-validate and board—no ticket inspection.

Book online at 30direct.com or pay €10 on board. Book in advance for €9 rate.

To board: Show your ticket to the driver (printed, phone e-ticket, or mobile). Tickets can be purchased directly from the driver. Visa/Mastercard accepted onboard (American Express not accepted).

About BikeTourFrance.net
Eat. Sleep. Roll. Repeat.
I'm John, the cyclist behind BikeTourFrance.net. I help riders carry out extraordinary bicycle tours in France.

I personally lead four very small, self-supported group tours each year. Groups have no more than twelve riders, so I can lead the ride, explain each day's plan in depth, and give the group the attention it needs.

If you prefer to travel on your own schedule, I offer a self-guided tour package. I build the routes, book your accommodations, and give practical support as you prepare for the trip.
How the tours work

All BikeTourFrance.net tours are self-supported. You carry your own gear from place to place. The Canal des Deux Mers is fairly flat, so you do not need to obsess over every gram, but space still matters. Pack less than you think you need.

Planning a bicycle tour in France gets complex fast. Where you ride, how far you go, where you eat, where you sleep, how trains fit in, and when you stop to see a place all affect one another. A small choice early in the plan can cause a hard day later.
Who is planning your trip

I have planned and ridden self-supported tours across France, and I have traveled on foot in many parts of the country. I know what works on the ground: routes that make sense, days that fit real riders, places to stay, food stops, train options, and the small details that keep a trip moving well. I also know that coordinating your arrival time with your lodging makes a big difference for everyone.

Outside of touring, I lead rides for Cascade Bicycle Club in Seattle, work in enterprise technology, and hold DELF B2 certification in French. I'm not a camper. I like a good route, a real bed, a warm shower, and a solid meal at the end of the day. It is France, after all, and I love to eat well.

This page describes what this website does today. Last updated October 2, 2026.

## What this website collects

This website has no sign-up form, no account system, and no analytics or advertising tools. It does not set cookies of its own. See the [Cookies page](/cookies/).

## When you email John

If you write to [contact@biketourfrance.net](mail:general), John receives your message and your email address in his BikeTourFrance.net email account. He uses them to reply to you. Nothing in this website's code sends your message anywhere else.

## Hosting and technical logs

Web servers normally record technical details of each visit, such as the page requested and the visitor's IP address. This website is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, which handles those records. John does not receive a copy of them through this website.

## Other sites and media

The Resources page loads audio files from BikeTourFrance.net's media storage only when you press play. It also links to Google Docs and Google Sheets and to other websites. Those sites have their own privacy practices.

## Questions

Write to [contact@biketourfrance.net](mail:general).
